title: Cold to Go: Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography to Investigate the Nanoscale Solid–Liquid Interfaces of SnSe Anodes for Next-Generation Batteries
content: Improving the performance and lifetime of liquid-electrolyte-based batteries, especially the widely used Li-ion systems, requires a comprehensive understanding of the nanoscale interactions at the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) between the electrode and the electrolyte [1, 2]. Characterizing this region is inherently challenging due to the volatile and liquid nature of the electrolytes, which are easily disturbed during conventional preparation methods. Techniques such as electrode washing can irreparably damage the sensitive SEI, while other approaches lack the resolution or chemical specificity necessary to capture key nanoscale processes [3].
